dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Pense: quantas vezes o número 5 cabe inteiramente dentro do 12?
Tente subtrair 5 de 12 uma vez, e depois outra vez. Quantas vezes você conseguiu subtrair 5 e quanto sobrou de resto?
Você subtraiu 5 duas vezes, então a parte inteira (m1) é 2. Agora, olhe para o resto que sobrou: esse é o seu novo numerador (m2).
O denominador (m3) continua sendo 5. Se você tirou dois grupos de 5 (que dá 10), quanto falta para chegar em 12? Esse valor vai no campo m2.
Onde o número 2 e 2/5 se localiza entre os números inteiros 2 e 3?
A reta está dividida em 5 partes entre cada número inteiro. Conte duas dessas pequenas marcas após o número 2.
Se cada marca vale 1/5, onde a segunda marca depois do 2 se encontra?
Coloque o ponto exatamente na segunda marcação após o número 2. Você consegue ver as divisões?

Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: In a fraction, the numerator tells how many parts or pieces are being counted.
Look for the quantity Brandon gave to his friends and place that quantity in the top field.
The top field represents the total number of gum pieces given away, not the number of pieces in one pack.
Read the number of pieces Brandon gave away and type that number into f1.
The denominator tells how many equal pieces make one whole pack.
Find the number of gum pieces in one pack and enter it in the bottom field.
Use the pieces-per-pack information, not the total number of pieces Brandon gave away.
Type the number of pieces in one pack into f2.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator represents more than one complete denominator-sized group.
Compare the number of pieces given away with the number of pieces in one full pack.
Ask whether the total pieces can make at least one complete pack and still have pieces remaining.
After deciding that the fraction exceeds one, press the button labeled ....
A mixed number combines complete packs with the fractional part of another pack.
Divide the total pieces by the pieces in one pack; use the quotient for the whole-number part and the remainder for the fractional numerator.
Count how many complete groups of five fit into twelve, then identify how many pieces remain.
Enter the number of complete packs in m1, the leftover pieces in m2, and keep the one-pack denominator in m3.
A point on the number line shows the value of the fraction as a location between whole numbers.
Use the mixed-number form to locate the point after the second whole number.
Each unit interval is divided into five equal parts, so use the appropriate fifths position after 2.
Start at 2 and move four of the five equal subdivisions toward 3, then place the point there.
Before finishing, check that the marked location represents the same value as the fraction.
Compare the point with the mixed-number location and verify that it lies between 2 and 3.
Make sure the point is on the fourth of the five equal subdivisions after 2.
When the point is correctly positioned, select the button labeled ... to submit the task.

exercicio.statement:
What if Brandon shared more gum? Let's say each pack had five pieces and he gave his friends a total of 12 pieces. Describe the number of packs of gum Brandon gave away and show the value on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

In field f2, enter the denominator of the fraction.
Use the fraction model to recognize that the fraction is greater than one, then click Convert.
Complete the mixed-number fields in the rightFraction group.
On the number line from 0 to 3, mark the point equivalent to 12/5.
After checking the point at 2.4, click Done.

When the point is correctly positioned, select the button labeled ... to submit the task.

nodes.instruction: You found the two complete packs but treated the division as if nothing remained. Record the leftover pieces in the fractional part.

nodes.instruction: Do not add the numerator and denominator to create the mixed fraction. Use groups of five to find the complete packs and the remainder.
